messages:
maria: Heads-up — running into a blind spot with quota attribution when requests are impersonated via SA proxies. Users see the project billed but no clear breadcrumbs in the console.
jamal: Can you paste an example? is it happening for both Dedicated and Hosted?
maria: Hosted for now. Sequence: client API key -> proxy service (impersonates SA) -> inference. Console shows client project as owner of usage. No link to the SA or proxy service.
ben: That sounds like origin vs effective-identity confusion. We currently surface 'requesting project' and 'billing project' but not 'effective principal'.
ava: Is the problem mostly QA/console visibility or does it affect quota enforcement too?
maria: Both. Quota enforcement is correct (it charges project A) but telemetry/alerts group by the original API key project, so on-call gets noisy signals.
jamal: Oof. So the alerting noise is coming from routing/telemetry aggregation. We tag by incoming key by default.
sre-bot: New reminder: any change to quota-tagging must preserve historical continuity for billing dashboards.
ben: Proposal: add an "effective_principal" tag in metrics (service_account:projects/PROJECT/sa/NAME) and a console column that links to the SA. Keep incoming_key_project as fallback.
ava: Agree, but we should be careful about exposing SAs cross-org in the UI. Need an access check before showing link.
maria: We can show it only to users who have view access on the SA's org/project. For others, show a blurred badge with hover tooltip: "requires access to view principal".
jamal: Implementation notes: instrumentation change in auth-proxy to emit both origin_project and effective_principal in request trace header: `X-RW-Origin: proj:123` and `X-RW-Effective: sa:proj-xyz/rt-sa`. Then runtime/pipeline attaches both to metrics.
ben: Telemetry storage: add a secondary dimension `effective_principal` to our metering pipeline. We need to watch cardinality. Many ephemeral SAs could blow up cardinality.
ava: Maybe only surface the top N principals in the UI and roll smaller ones into "other". For alerts, allow rule to pick either origin or effective.
maria: Rollout plan idea: 1) emit header + metric tag (no UI) for 2 weeks, 2) add console column behind flag, 3) enable in alerts by opt-in.
jamal: How do we avoid breaking existing billing reports? Make sure billing ETL ignores the new tag unless explicitly switched.
ben: Agreed. Also add a mapping job to reconcile existing traces — so we can backfill effective_principal for recent data when available.
ava: UX: add a quick 'who-used-my-project' filter that can switch between origin vs effective view. That helps customers debug impersonation leaks.
maria: Edgecase: proxy may chain multiple impersonations. We should persist the last effective principal only. Add `impersonation_chain` length metric for ops.
jamal: Good call. For quota enforcement we keep current behaviour (attr to billing project) — only change telemetry/visibility.
sre-bot: Flagged for RFC: "impersonation-metrics-and-console-visibility". Please include perf impact estimates for metric cardinality.
ben: I'll prototype metric keys: `rw.request.count{origin_project, effective_principal, model, route}` and run a sample on last 30d logs to estimate unique SA count.
maria: Thanks — can we aim to flip the header emission on for all hosts next week behind internal flag? Then collect telemetry for 48h.
ava: I'll draft the console mock with privacy gating.
jamal: Thx team. If anyone hits a regression in alerting after header flag on, ping #eng-oncall immediately and rollback.
maria: I'll post the RFC link once Ben has the numbers. :+1:
